purpose: Answer the throttle and ETA questions put to lane C, from commands run in one turn. Every count here comes from a command in that turn, per BEN-027 -- and the authority-vs-symptom rule of BEN-233, so the throttle is READ from the setting rather than inferred from occupancy.

observed.both_clocks_printed_deliberately: BEN-233: sacct prints local time, and mixing it with `date -u` made me nearly report a 7-hour collapse that never happened.

THE_THROTTLE_ANSWER.question_as_put: 'Throttle is 2 ... was 2 deliberate? If it was only caution, raising it is worth ~hours.'
THE_THROTTLE_ANSWER.answer: THE THROTTLE IS 10 AND ALWAYS WAS. It was never 2.
corroborated_by: the submission receipt: gate5-extraction-r2-active-56936015.json records array.concurrency_cap = 10
THE_THROTTLE_ANSWER.what_2_actually_was: OBSERVED OCCUPANCY, not a configured cap. Every pending task reported (Priority) -- queue contention, not our own limit.
THE_THROTTLE_ANSWER.and_it_has_since_RAMPED: 7 tasks are RUNNING right now (19,20,21,22,23,24,25) across 5 nodes. The contention eased on its own; nothing was changed.
THE_THROTTLE_ANSWER.so_the_proposed_fix_is_a_no_op: raising the cap cannot help: the cap is 10, Slurm is currently granting 7 of it, and the binding constraint was scheduling priority. There is nothing to take to Joseph.

THE_ETA_ANSWER.measurement_note: squeue -j 56936015 -r -h gives the per-task truth (24 PENDING). sacct -X COMPRESSES the pending array range into ONE row and reports PENDING 1 -- a 24x under-report, and the reason the campaign rule says squeue -r for per-task counts.
THE_ETA_ANSWER.supersedes_my_earlier_estimate: I said ~5 hours when concurrency was ~2. That was right for the rate then and is now wrong: the rate is a scheduling outcome, not a property of the job, so any ETA built on it expires when contention changes. Stated as a lesson rather than a correction, because it will happen again.
THE_ETA_ANSWER.then: family validator 56936016 releases on afterany:56936015 and must report exactly 50/50 GATE5_EXTRACTION_FAMILY_COMPLETE_PASS

A_PREMISE_I_HAVE_TO_CORRECT.the_claim: 'the Gate-6 floor's last draw has now been queued 30 hours behind our own array' -- put to me twice as the reason the throttle mattered.
A_PREMISE_I_HAVE_TO_CORRECT.measured: 56863958_5 (g6_floor) is RUNNING, on nid001425. It is not starved and it is not waiting behind this array.
A_PREMISE_I_HAVE_TO_CORRECT.why_it_matters: the throttle question was framed as a tradeoff against a starved Gate-6 floor. There is no tradeoff: the floor is running, and our cap is not the constraint on either job. Both halves of the premise were wrong, and acting on it would have been a change with no benefit made for a reason that did not hold.
A_PREMISE_I_HAVE_TO_CORRECT.this_is_BEN_233_again_from_the_other_sid: a number inferred from a symptom (the floor was pending when last looked at) rather than read from the thing that sets it (its current state).

CAN_EXTRACTION_FAIL_LATE_IN_A_WAY_THE_FI.answer: Yes, in three ways, and none is speculative -- each is a mechanism already present in this campaign.
CAN_EXTRACTION_FAIL_LATE_IN_A_WAY_THE_FI.1_per_member_mask_flicker: the reporting mask is a per-replica DRAW (BEN-231). The never-reported set can only SHRINK and the flicker set can only GROW as members arrive, so a cell reported in all 19 today can still fail at member 37. The union/intersection counts are therefore BOUNDS, not values -- which is why the spec marks every such number [N=14] and requires re-measurement at 50/50.
CAN_EXTRACTION_FAIL_LATE_IN_A_WAY_THE_FI.2_the_shared_output_root: the FAILED r1 array 56935552 and this array write to the SAME root. r1 wrote no products, so nothing is contaminated -- but that is luck, and it is why CSTAT-R3e (member digests) and CSTAT-R3f (constant slurm_array_job_id) are required rather than advisory.
CAN_EXTRACTION_FAIL_LATE_IN_A_WAY_THE_FI.3_wall_limit_vs_a_slow_task: tasks run ~14.5 min against a 2h limit, so there is 8x headroom -- but task 0 finished in 2:05 because it REUSED the predecessor's complete push. A member whose push must be rebuilt from scratch costs the full price, and the ones with no reusable push are the later indices.
CAN_EXTRACTION_FAIL_LATE_IN_A_WAY_THE_FI.what_would_NOT_be_hidden: a crash, a schema mismatch, a coverage failure, or a factor-inventory mismatch -- those fail loudly and per-task, and 19 of 19 have passed them.
